To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the probability of new ultrafine particle generation of CCN varies throughout different regions of the atmosphere and that uncertainties in primary aerosol size distributions can have large effects on the number of CCNs generated.

the probability of an ultrafine particle growing to a CCN is highly variable and depends on the local atmospheric conditions, the uncertainty in the primary emissions size distribution is the largest uncertainty in predicting the CCN generated by ultrafine particles and the number of CCNs ultimately generated is not a robust function of the total mass or number of primary ultrafine particles.

the efficiency of CCN formation from ultrafine aerosol depends on the size distribution of primary emissions, the concentrations of condensation nuclei and condensable species, and the deposition velocity of the aerosol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how new particles are formed and how efficiently they grow to become CCNs in different parts of our atmosphere.
the growth and sinks of new ultrafine aerosol and the efficiency of CCN generation from ultrafine particles in different parts of atmosphere.
the growth and removal of new aerosol particles, and how these processes affect their ability to form cloud condensation nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCN formation is very sensitive to the size of the particles, and the size of ultrafine particles can be very different from the size of the primary particles.
the probability of an ultrafine particle generating CCN depends on the atmospheric region and on the size distribution of the primary emissions.
the efficiency of new ultrafine particle growth varies greatly throughout the atmosphere and is highly uncertain, making it difficult to predict the effect of ultrafine particle emissions on CCN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PUG model is a useful tool for assessing the efficiency of CCN formation from ultrafine particle emissions and that the PUG results are useful for assessing the uncertainties in CCN generation in global aerosol microphysical models.
the probability of an ultrafine particle growing to become a CCN depends on a large number of factors and that the uncertainty of the number of particles that become CCN is high.
ultrafine particles have significant potential to form CCN, but the efficiency of this conversion depends on the details of the atmospheric chemistry and microphysics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not possible to simply state that a certain fraction of ultrafine particle emissions will grow to become CCNs.
CCN formation from ultrafine aerosol is highly variable, but in most cases a large fraction of the ultrafine aerosol will grow to CCN.

CCN formation from ultrafine particle growth is a stochastic process and that the uncertainty in the number and size distribution of new ultrafine particle emissions is a significant source of uncertainty in CCN formation.
